# Other Node.js Core Modules

> Part of the [Implementation Status](README.md) index. Smaller or lower-priority Node built-in modules, grouped here rather than given a full page each. Split out to its own page (rather than [PROCESS-CLI.md](PROCESS-CLI.md)) once it's substantial enough to need one.

**Coverage**: 16/17 (~94%) · **Strict Coverage**: 3/17 (~18%).

Format: [Status page format](README.md#status-page-format).

| `assert` | ✅ | • No `assert.CallTracker` (deprecated in Node, DEP0173)<br>• Deep equality does not compare symbol-keyed properties, and a failure diff does not invoke getters (Node's `getters: true`)<br>• An uncaught `AssertionError` prints `Uncaught: <message>`; Node prints `AssertionError [ERR_ASSERTION]: <message>`, its stack and its properties | • Node's lib/assert.js in TypeScript (`lib/node/assert.ts`, with `AssertionError`, the Myers diff and `isDeepStrictEqual` ported alongside): every assertion, `rejects`/`doesNotReject`, `partialDeepStrictEqual`, the `Assert` class, and `assert/strict`; messages, diffs and `ok`'s quoted call source match Node's ([ADR-01288](../adr/ADR-01288.md))<br>• Colours follow stderr as Node's do: plain unless it is a terminal that shows them |

Expected exactly N, actual M.`), `mustSucceed` (asserts no error, then calls with the rest), `mustNotCall`, `expectsError`, `expectWarning`, `skip` (`1..0 # Skipped: …`, exit 0), and the platform probes — alongside the runner's functions |
